what: Where the full scored path saturates above 500 authorizations a second, and why
follows: bench/full_path_repeat_2026-10-22.json (4 scorer workers x 1 thread with the TCP_NODELAY fix, the Compose default)
hardware: Apple M3 Pro, 11 cores, 18 GiB; Docker Desktop VM with 11 CPUs and 11.67 GiB; k6 2.3.0 natively on the same Mac
method: Each run on a fresh Compose project (payguard_bench) with new volumes, a 15 s warm-up at 100/s, then a measured 15 s run of bench/load_full.js. During each run pg_stat_activity was sampled about every 0.4 s for the API's connections and docker stats was sampled continuously; both samplers add some load of their own. Single runs per setting.

host_cpu_at_800.top: macOS top during the run: 0.8% and 1.9% idle; Docker's VM process 546% and 723%; k6 144% and 49%

scorer_in_process_ms.what: Median and p99 of 2,000 in-process calls with threads=1, no HTTP, empty card history

findings: 600 and 700/s completed every scheduled authorization with no errors, but with a heavy tail (p99 about 400 ms) and about 2.5% rules fallback.

750/s is the knee: all 20 pooled connections were in use (16 idle in transaction, waiting on the scorer), p50 jumped to 459 ms and k6 dropped 318 iterations. At 850/s throughput fell to about 620 completed per second.
6 or 8 scorer workers instead of 4 raised 850/s throughput by about 10% only; scorer CPU stayed near 285% regardless.

The host itself was out of CPU: about 800% of container CPU plus k6, with macOS reporting 1-2% idle at 800/s. The ceiling of roughly 730/s on this laptop is total CPU shared by every service and the load generator, not one component.
At 750/s the stack spent about 11 ms of CPU per authorization: scorer 3.7 ms, API 2.4 ms, PostgreSQL 1.5 ms, Kafka 1.4 ms, outbox 0.7 ms.

In process a score costs 0.61 ms, 0.56 ms of it LightGBM TreeSHAP for the reason codes. Alone at 500/s the scorer container used 1.2 ms of CPU per request, so serving adds about 0.6 ms; the ~3.7 ms per authorization seen at saturation is mostly the cost of CPU contention, not serving code.
next: Run the load generator on a separate machine so it does not compete for the CPU it measures.

Lower CPU per authorization across services: TreeSHAP only where reason codes are shown (about half of the scorer's own 1.2 ms), and re-test httptools/uvloop with more repeats (6-18% on the scorer alone).
Give Kafka and the outbox a CPU budget check; together they use about 2 ms of CPU per authorization.
limits: One machine; the samplers add load; single runs per setting.
Synthetic workload and model; not a production capacity claim.

scorer_alone_500_per_s.what: k6 sending the same request mix straight to the scorer at 500/s for 20 s, with only Redis and the scorer running (4 workers x 1 thread); docker stats sampled 10 times during each run. Order: base, fast, base, fast, each on a fresh project.
scorer_alone_500_per_s.reading: Alone, the scorer used 1.2 ms of CPU per request, of which 0.61 ms is the in-process score; HTTP, FastAPI/pydantic and the Redis lookup add about 0.6 ms. In the saturated full stack the same container used about 3.7 ms per authorization, so CPU contention roughly tripled the cost per request. The C HTTP parser and uvloop cut the scorer-alone cost by 18% in one pair and 6% in the other: too small and inconsistent to adopt on this evidence.
